// Expected values for the pig farmer's work (docs/rules/pig-farming.md), captured from the original program in the emulator (ADR 0008):
// tools/GhidraDump/emulate.py, the verb goods with a finished pig farm (type 14, a large building) at a flag, reduced to the passes that
// matter. The building's flag pointer (+0xe, which its handler 0x42e0fa keeps its grain request through) is set by hand, as a built site
// leaves it (0x43ef82). The verb also runs 0x44579c before the castle, as the player setup of a new game does, so the rank of the grain
// request starts from the original's word (the high byte of +0x158). The pig farm's handler has no preamble that loads the player block, so
// it reads the pointer the code before it left: the part castle-off@300 of the command sets the castle's building type (whose handler, not
// ported, leaves other pointers) to 0 before the pass 300, after the worker is inside, so that the rank is the player's (docs/rules/
// pig-farming.md, "The rank"). A scenario starts with a "#" line that names its verb command; each line after it gives, for a pass, the 16
// bytes of the pig farmer (slot 3, s3=: a settler without a job that the castle makes the pig farmer) where his node or part of the work
// changed (the work's lines only where his stretch changed), the 18 bytes of the building (b=, its flag pointer left out) where they
// changed, the flag's byte 4 and goods bytes (g=) where they changed, the request words of the flag (req=, the bytes 0x42 to 0x45) where
// they changed, the castle's grain count (grain=) and pig count (pig=) where they changed, and the generator's words (rng=) as they
// stand. The puts of the command lay the grains on the places of the castle's flag (slot 1) or of another flag by hand. The flags are
// listed in the order the engine numbers them (by column). The one-grain scenario runs to the castle's first pig, at the pass 12709. At
// the pass 98 the request words show the rank 0, which the castle's leftover pointer gives (the engine writes 0 while the worker is on the
// way). Not production code: no routine of the program is transcribed here, only values the program produced.
